title: The prayer of seeking guidance
hookLine: two units and a du'a when deciding (Bukhari)

cards: Two job offers sit in two browser tabs. Or it's a lease, a move back home, a person a family has suggested, or whether to say yes to a surgery. A list of pros and cons has been written twice and torn up once.

A companion named Jabir said the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught them a prayer for exactly this, in all their affairs, the way he taught them a surah of the Qur'an. Not only the huge decisions. All of them.

teach.b: Istikharah means asking God to choose the good. First, the form, from the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari: when one of you is concerned about a matter, pray two units that are not the obligatory prayer, then make this du'a.

Second, the words, described rather than recited here. The person asks God to choose for them by His knowledge and give them ability by His power, because God has power and they have none, God knows and they do not.

teach.h: IF IT'S GOOD, MAKE IT EASY.
teach.b: Then the heart of it: if this matter, named here, is good for me in my religion, my living and how my affairs turn out, decree it for me and make it easy.
If it is bad for me, turn it away from me, and turn me away from it. Then decree the good for me wherever it is, and make me content with it. It doesn't only ask for the right door.
It asks to be at peace with whichever door opens. Third, what the hadith doesn't say.

It mentions no dream, no sign in the sky, no rush of certainty. Scholars describe the answer in different ways. Some say go ahead with what you were leaning toward and watch whether the way is made easy or blocked.
Some speak of the heart settling. Some advise pairing it with asking people you trust. Fourth, why hand a choice over.
Pickthall's translation of surah two: "it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not."
Istikharah doesn't stop the person deciding.
It changes who they're deciding with.

how: Muslims facing a decision pray two voluntary units and then recite the istikharah du'a taught in Sahih al-Bukhari, naming the matter in it; then they go ahead, often after asking advice from people they trust.

o: asking God to choose the good, with two units and a du'a
asking family elders to make a hard choice for you
waiting for a dream or sign that settles a decision

games.q: the prayer of seeking guidance — tap the pairs.
p: taught it like a surah of the Qur'an
asking God to choose the good
if it is bad for me
turn it away, and turn me from it

s: the hadith promises a dream after istikharah
it mentions no dream or sign. scholars describe the answer in several ways.
it was taught for all affairs, not only huge ones
Jabir said he taught it in all their affairs, as he taught a surah.
the du'a asks to be made content with what is decreed
it ends: decree the good wherever it is, and make me content with it.

games.q: you've prayed istikharah about a move. no dream, no sign. what does the hadith tell you to wait for?
o: nothing: it promises no sign at all.
a stranger to tell you the answer.
games.why: the hadith gives the prayer and the du'a, and promises no sign. some scholars say go ahead and see whether the way is made easy.

practice: Bring one real choice to mind and hold each option in turn, noticing your shoulders, your jaw, your stomach, without deciding.

If you pray, you can pray two units today and make the istikharah du'a in the hadith's words, learned from a teacher or a trusted book. If you don't, sit with the choice and loosen your grip on it, open to either answer.

wordCard.voice: Istikharah. Asking God to choose the good: two voluntary units, then a du'a that asks for the good and for contentment with it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: seeking the good choice, asking God to choose. it shares its root with khayr, good.

carryVoice: Your line: choose for me. The du'a asks for peace with whichever door opens. Until tomorrow.
